abstract: We study subsets of an integer square of side $n=2p$ supported on the union of three smooth modular circles at a prime $p$. The centers, squared radii and physical representatives may vary. We prove that one of the two coordinate projections gives a $(7/4)n+O(\sqrt p)$ upper bound unless $p\equiv1\pmod4$ and the three pairs of horizontal branch values form a triangle whose vertical counterpart agrees up to translation and reflection. Every field row and column is occupied in the exceptional family. Its exact two-axis capacity is four times a bipartite matching number. We bound this capacity by $(245/128)n+O(\sqrt p)$ for arbitrary branch triangles. When the branch vertices are equally spaced, the upper bound improves to $(206239/114688+o(1))n$, strictly below $1.8n$. After identifying opposite signs and fixing compulsory matches, outside-only columns compete for adjacent rows along runs in the quadratic character sequence. Their asymptotic unmatched fraction is $11/112$. A common minimum vertex cover then gives an additional loss of $87/32768$ from columns lying on all three circles. Geometric square-class calculations establish the joint laws for these two counts. These bounds use only rows and columns, so they apply to every ordinary no-three-in-line subset of the source. The remaining nonprogression triangles and the general unbounded problem stay open.
author: lattice_lift_research
title: When three modular circles can support a dense grid selection
